result.summary: Implemented docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md exactly as designed, no schema change (confirmed by the design's own §0 statement, DATA-DESIGNER not dispatched). 1. apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts: NEW isAutoPromotionHalted(startsAt, evaluationTime) per design §2.1 -- pure, evaluationTime an explicit parameter (decisions/0006), placed alongside isFinished/isRegistrationOpen. True (halted) when 24h or less remain before startsAt, including the exact T-24h instant; false (allowed) when strictly more than 24h remain. 2. apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts: - NEW decidePromotionEligibility (§2.2, pure, no I/O): first-match-wins table -- eventStatus!=='published' OR isFinished -> 'event-not-eligible'; isAutoPromotionHalted -> 'halted-t24h'; seatsLeft<=0 -> 'capacity-full'; else ok:true. Implemented in the exact stated row order. - NEW promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible(tx, eventId, evaluationTime) (§3, the transactional actor): step 1 SELECT events FOR UPDATE as the FIRST operation (never opens its own db.transaction -- always reuses the caller's tx); step 2 fresh admittedCount read + computeSeatsLeft; step 3 decidePromotionEligibility, returning early on any refusal with zero further reads/writes; step 4 SELECT the earliest-created waitlisted row via the exact (created_at ASC, id ASC) tie-break getWaitlistPosition already established (REQ-021), FOR UPDATE, LIMIT 1 -- empty waitlist returns {kind:'no-waitlist'}, no error; step 5 UPDATE naming only admission/qr_token in its SET clause; step 6 exactly one writeAuditLog call (actorUserId: null, action='registration.promote'), same tx as step 5's UPDATE; step 7 returns {kind:'promoted', registrationId, promotedUserId, qrToken}. - withdrawRegistration extended per design §0: captures the pre-withdrawal admission (wasAdmitted) before the UPDATE overwrites it; after the existing withdraw UPDATE + audit write, calls promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible(tx, row.eventId, at) ONLY when wasAdmitted was true, using the SAME tx (atomic with the withdrawal); returns {kind:'withdrawn', promotion} instead of bare {kind:'withdrawn'}, where promotion is {kind:'not-attempted'} when step 6 was skipped. - WithdrawOutcome's 'withdrawn' member extended to carry `promotion: PromotionOutcome`, per design §4. decideWithdrawOutcome (pure, no I/O, unchanged signature) necessarily supplies the fixed {kind:'not-attempted'} sentinel on its own 'withdrawn' return -- it cannot know the real promotion outcome without I/O; no caller of decideWithdrawOutcome inspects .promotion on that branch (the command handler's §4.1 step 5 only branches on outcome.kind), so this is purely a type-level necessity, not a behavior change. Flagged in issues below as a minor design-gap finding since the design's §4 literal type didn't address this pure-function conflict explicitly. - NEW getEventIdForRegistration(db, registrationId): plumbing read (not named by the design, mechanical necessity) letting the confirm-callback handler resolve the withdrawn registration's own eventId for the promotion notification's event title/date-time composition -- plain SELECT, no lock, no business logic. 3. apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts: NEW getUserForNotificationById(db, userId) per design §6.1 -- resolves tgId/lang/chapterDefaultLang starting FROM an internal users.id (the promoted person, a different Telegram user than ctx.from), same join shape as getFlowUserByTgId filtered by users.id instead of tg_id. 4. apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts: makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler extended per design §6.2 -- after withdrawRegistration returns and answerCallbackQuery, when outcome.kind==='withdrawn' and outcome.promotion.kind==='promoted', calls a new sendPromotionNotification helper: resolves the promoted person via getUserForNotificationById (defensive null-tgId guard, no error surfaced), resolves THEIR OWN language via resolveLang (never the withdrawer's), composes [promotion.admittedPrefix, eventTitle, dateTimeText, qrLabel+qrToken, promotion.whatNext] exactly per design §6.3, and sends via ctx.api.sendMessage(promotedTgId, text) -- the one call site in this codebase addressing a chat other than the current update's own. No broadcast_opt_in check anywhere in this path (S10). This send never blocks or affects the withdrawer's own confirmedReply, which is sent unconditionally afterward regardless of promotion outcome. 5. i18n: new Catalog.promotion section (admittedPrefix/whatNext/qrLabel) added to apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts per design §6.3 -- placeholder/minimal functional copy per decisions/0002, CONTENT-BA owns final wording. catalogs.test.ts required no change. Test additions -- apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts gained: decidePromotionEligibility (6 pure cases, no DB, covering every row of the first-match-wins table including T-24h checked before capacity); decideWithdrawOutcome's existing 'withdrawn' case updated to expect the {kind:'not-attempted'} sentinel; 3 pre-existing withdrawRegistration DB tests updated to expect the real promotion outcome ('no-waitlist' where no waitlist existed) instead of the old bare {kind:'withdrawn'}; REQ-023 AC1 (48h-out event, capacity full, 3 distinct-created_at waitlisted rows -- withdrawal promotes exactly the earliest, confirmed by id/promotedUserId/fresh qr_token, other two rows read back unchanged); AC2 (12h-out event -- withdrawal outcome is exactly {kind:'withdrawn', promotion:{kind:'halted-t24h'}}, waitlisted row unchanged, admitted-count stays 0); AC3 (empty waitlist -- {kind:'withdrawn', promotion:{kind:'no-waitlist'}}, no error); AC4 (20-iteration real-concurrency test: withdrawRegistration racing a fresh registerForEvent call for the SAME capacity-1 freed seat via Promise.all -- asserts admitted-row count is always exactly 1, never 2, in every iteration, and exactly one of {promotion succeeded, fresh registration admitted} is ever true, never both); AC5 (2 cases: promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible called directly against a cancelled event and against a finished event, both refuse with {kind:'event-not-eligible'}, waitlisted row read back unchanged); AC7 (2 cases: a successful promotion writes exactly one registration.promote audit row -- total new rows = 2, one withdraw + one promote; running promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible twice against a still-full event both times returns {kind:'capacity-full'} with zero audit writes either time, both waitlisted rows untouched). apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts gained REQ-023 AC6 (real grammY dispatch: confirming a withdrawal that frees a capacity-1 seat sends exactly 3 captured calls -- answerCallbackQuery, sendMessage to the PROMOTED person's own chat_id (verified via payload.chat_id, with their broadcast_opt_in explicitly set false beforehand to prove S10's transactional-ignores-the-flag rule), then sendMessage as the withdrawer's own confirmedReply; the promoted row is confirmed admitted with a fresh qr_token). AC verification, all against a real scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, migrated via drizzle-kit migrate): AC1 PASS, AC2 PASS, AC3 PASS, AC4 PASS (20/20 iterations, 672ms, admitted-row count never exceeded 1, exactly-one-of-two-fills-the-seat held every iteration), AC5 PASS (both cancelled and finished-event refusals), AC6 PASS (notification sent to promoted person's own chat regardless of broadcast_opt_in=false, verified via real grammY handleUpdate() dispatch), AC7 PASS (exactly one audit_log row per promotion; a re-run against a still-full event sends nothing). REQ-020 CONCURRENCY REGRESSION CHECK (explicitly re-run per this task's instruction): re-ran registration.db.test.ts's pre-existing 'registerForEvent -- AC1: atomic capacity under real concurrency' test (20 iterations) individually with -t filter and --reporter=verbose: PASS, unchanged behavior -- exactly one of two concurrent registerForEvent calls admitted per iteration, confirming this run's additions (a second FOR UPDATE lock-taker on the events table, promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible) did not disturb registerForEvent's own pre-existing locking. Commands run from the REPO ROOT (never --root apps/bot): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings, unchanged). `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces; apps/web Next.js build succeeded, apps/bot's `tsc -p tsconfig.json` clean with zero errors (this required one fix beyond the design's literal text: decideWithdrawOutcome's pure 'withdrawn' return needed the {kind:'not-attempted'} promotion sentinel to satisfy WithdrawOutcome's extended type -- see issues below). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 17 files / 211 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. 211 = REQ-022's own confirmed baseline of 196 + 15 new cases (14 in registration.db.test.ts + 1 in handlers/withdraw.test.ts). Individually re-ran registration.db.test.ts (45/45 green, includes AC4's 672ms concurrency run) and handlers/withdraw.test.ts (5/5 green, includes AC6) with --reporter=verbose to confirm every case actually executed against live Postgres. Scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432) was started fresh for this run (was not already running) and left running for REVIEWER/TEST-RUNNER's convenience -- not torn down. `git status --porcelain` confirms only the 9 modified files listed in artifacts_out are dirty, all under apps/bot/**; no new files, no file touched outside apps/bot/**.

issues.title: REQ-023 design §4's WithdrawOutcome extension conflicts with decideWithdrawOutcome's purity, resolved with a sentinel rather than left unresolved
issues.description: Design §4 states WithdrawOutcome's 'withdrawn' member gains a mandatory `promotion: PromotionOutcome` field, and decideWithdrawOutcome's declared signature (unchanged per the design, `(input) => WithdrawOutcome`) is the SAME type. But decideWithdrawOutcome is a pure, no-I/O function that cannot know a real promotion outcome, which requires a DB transaction. TypeScript's structural check confirmed this conflict (`tsc` failed: 'Property promotion is missing'). Resolved by having decideWithdrawOutcome's own 'withdrawn' return supply the design's own {kind:'not-attempted'} sentinel value (the same value the design already defines for 'promotion was not attempted') -- this is a value already named by the design for exactly this situation, not an invented one, and no caller of decideWithdrawOutcome inspects .promotion on that branch. Filed as MINOR rather than routed back because the resolution uses only vocabulary the design itself already defines and does not touch any capacity/consent/who-sees-data rule; flagging so a future design pass either states this sentinel explicitly or gives decideWithdrawOutcome a narrower return type of its own (mirroring how RegisterForEventResult sits atop RegistrationOutcome rather than reusing it verbatim).
